Thanks! Looks like we are missing a conversion from `tensor.cast` to `hal.tensor.cast`. I am not sure why we even have `hal.tensor.cast` in the inputs in one place and `tensor.cast` in the other...

hal.tensor.cast is what we want on external ABI boundaries - it lets us explicitly specify the type moved across the program boundary (an `iree_hal_buffer_view_t`) and how to get its shape information. Internally within a module tensor.cast should be fine (though it doesn't carry shapes and is not a great op - it'd be better to have a variant that was like hal.tensor.cast as otherwise we'd need to insert things like the shapex.tie_shape stuff again to attach that information).
Ok, actually I feel like this op should not even make it into flow. Its actually losing shape information and seems like an intermediate IR state.

If this is a public function then we can do something like what we do with the [SavedModelToIreeABI](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/fbe4821c2a6d1f772cec74be0171c1e2db6b645f/integrations/tensorflow/iree_tf_compiler/TF/SavedModelToIreeABI.cpp) pass. That is what does this type casting on the tensorflow side, saying that tensorflow I/O comes into the module in as bufferviews or nested lists and other things that are frontend-specific and difficult/impossible to infer later on in the lowering. There's a generic version of this in [WrapEntryPoints](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/fbe4821c2a6d1f772cec74be0171c1e2db6b645f/iree/compiler/Bindings/Native/Transforms/WrapEntryPoints.cpp) that is used for generic inputs so `func(tensor) -> tensor` becomes `func(buffer_view) -> buffer_view` (iree-translate adds that with the `-iree-native-bindings-support` option).

If this is internal to the model then maybe a lowering to a flow.tensor.reshape could handle this.

There's two things going on here:
1. The tensor.cast op itself. As mentioned, it is really an identity, and e.g after doing per-dimension shape inference becomes a no-op, EXCEPT
2. At ABI boundaries, where we need to formally add/erase static type information to satisfy the function return type/function argument types

In npcomp, we run shape inference which eliminates almost all of these sorts of ops (this is actually still at the Torch level, this op comes in from TorchToLinalg, but the same idea applies), and then a pass which propagates the information to the ABI boundaries to eliminate the need for these formal ops. Doing that relies on the assumption that `tensor<4x4xf32>` and `tensor<?x?xf32>` are passed the same way from user API's, which is true for IREE (but is not true e.g. for some of the upstream weird calling conventions where memrefs get split into a C ABI as a raw pointer + a number of 'index' values equal to the number of `?`'s -- changing the number of `?`'s is an ABI-breaking change in that case)

Yeah - the ABI boundary is where we could handle these. We could, for example, extend WrapEntryPoints to look for these ops and replace them with the appropriate forms.

What we previously had was `func(tensor)` lowering deep into the HAL dialect before it decided to turn the tensors into `hal.buffer_view`, but that was a mess as then if targeting a different runtime API like you mention it isn't guaranteed to become that (tflite passes just unshaped buffers and sends shape information in a side-channel, for example). It can also hide information from the linalg/flow levels that want to better carry shape dimensions around as SSA values rooted up to input/down to output. 

The new approach is to specify what types you expect at runtime on the ABI boundary (like an `__attribute__((fastcall))` or `__attribute__((stdcall))` in C) and insert the placeholder conversion for them - in the case of `iree_hal_buffer_view_t` being passed adding a `hal.tensor.cast` to move between that type/shape-erased `!hal.buffer_view` into the `tensor<...>`. This avoids the ambiguity lower in the stack as the HAL knows precisely when it needs to materialize the buffer view types vs. when it's dealing with an internal tensor that it can treat as effectively just an offset into a ringbuffer with no runtime materialization at all. The bonus is that this also enables all the other kind of interop that may be desired - for example, passing in dicts for kwargs that are fetched and unpacked into primitives, custom types, and buffer_views without anything lower in the stack needing to somehow infer that - especially tricky for custom types/other dialect interaction.

So, now that we know there are two things - which are you hitting? Both I'm guessing?

I just looked, and I think it is mainly the ABI boundary one. I tried a 2 layer MLP but the tensor.cast ops end up disappearing through canonicalization currently. Probably more complex examples could result in tensor.cast ops that survive in the middle of the program, but that's not the immediate issue.

> I tried a 2 layer MLP but the tensor.cast ops end up disappearing through canonicalization currently.

It is useful to distinguish these "loopback" cases that just return an operand and functions that do real work. I've had to find/fix a number of the loopback cases that don't show up in real programs.
I think you are right about doing tensor_cast to HAL.tensor.cast early on for the public functions - we could make this part of WrapEntryPoints.
Note that this example shows up for a private function. I think we can just convert all such widening casts and rely on the fact that things have to line up for local dim resolution.

> It is useful to distinguish these "loopback" cases that just return an operand and functions that do real work. I've had to find/fix a number of the loopback cases that don't show up in real programs.

Sorry, my statement was not clear. Canonicalization removes all the tensor.cast ops in the program *except* the "ABI" tensor.cast at the end before the return. It's not specific to this loopback test case (you can see in my reduced test case it is called `%5` :) ).

I should have said

> I tried a 2 layer MLP but the [internal] tensor.cast ops end up disappearing through canonicalization currently.
@silvasean moving this back to you for now, till exact way forward is decided.
I assigned to me but have hours left before going offline for an extended period. Will see if a solution emerges.

Since landing the above requires an LLVM bump to avoid a mid-air collision, someone else will need to pick it up next week as I'll be out. Maybe Yi can finish/land it? I pushed it to a branch in the main repo so that others can push commits to it and merge.

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`tensor.cast` op doesn't seem to be supported

**To Reproduce**

Compile the following IR:
```
func @forward(%arg0: tensor<4x4xf32>) -> tensor<?x?xf32> {
  %5 = tensor.cast %arg0 : tensor<4x4xf32> to tensor<?x?xf32>
  return %5 : tensor<?x?xf32>
}
```

I see the error:
```
<stdin>:2:8: error: 'tensor.cast' op operand type '!hal.buffer_view' and result type 'tensor<?x?xf32>' are cast incompatible                                                                                      
  %5 = tensor.cast %arg0 : tensor<4x4xf32> to tensor<?x?xf32>
       ^
<stdin>:1:1: note: called from
func @forward(%arg0: tensor<4x4xf32>, %arg1: tensor<4x4xf32>) -> tensor<?x?xf32> {
^
<stdin>:0:0: error: conversion from source -> vm failed
```
issue.title: tensor.cast not working

* Fixes #6368 (verified on both the loopback and full MLP pastes).
* Should be finished/submitted once https://reviews.llvm.org/D105165 lands in IREE, since it adds new uses of memref.dim which it would be good to avoid mid-air collisions on. I left notes of what not to submit/change.

issue.body:
Reverts https://github.com/google/iree/pull/6648, rolling-forward https://github.com/google/iree/pull/6586. First commit is the pure revert, second is a set of proposed fixes for the performance regression. The single pass (with a true/false option) is now split further: * `createConvertTensorOpsPass` * `createConvertLinalgTensorOpsPass(true)` * `createConvertLinalgTensorOpsPass(false)` --- This gets the original change closer to an NFC (but it is still not an NFC). Before this change: | stage | patterns | | --- | --- | | `buildCommonInputConversionPassPipeline` | `tensor::CastOp`, `tensor::FromElementsOp` | | Flow, before DispatchRegionFormation | `tensor::InsertSliceOp`, `tensor::ExtractSliceOp`,
`linalg::TensorCollapseShapeOp`, `linalg::TensorExpandShapeOp` | | Flow, after DispatchRegionFormation | `linalg::FillOp` | After this change: | stage | patterns | | --- | --- | | `buildCommonInputConversionPassPipeline` | (deleted) | | Flow, before DispatchRegionFormation | `tensor::CastOp`, `tensor::FromElementsOp`,
`tensor::InsertSliceOp`, `tensor::ExtractSliceOp`,
`linalg::TensorCollapseShapeOp`, `linalg::TensorExpandShapeOp` | | Flow, after DispatchRegionFormation | `linalg::FillOp` | Passes on `linalg` ops are the same, but two `tensor` ops are now converted after linalg fusion, rather than at input conversion time. The first version of this change had those `linalg` ops converted during the "common input conversion pipeline".
